question.worked_solution:
First, note that $q=0$ cannot be a solution since division by $0$ is undefined. 

To solve the equation, we first apply cross-multiplication:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} & =\frac{1}{4q} \\ 1\cdot 4q & =2\cdot 1 \\ 4q & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we apply the multiplication principle:

$$
\begin{aligned}4q & =2 \\ \frac{4q}{4} & =\frac{2}{4} \\ q & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Since  $q=\frac{1}{2}$ is different from $q=0,$ we can accept it as a solution. Thus, the solution is $q=\frac{1}{2}.$
